bull.b: T-Mobile’s substantial operating and free cash flow provides durable funding for network investment, spectrum, dividends, and buybacks. The improvement from earlier periods, together with operating cash flow exceeding net income, indicates stronger earnings quality and supports financial resilience over the coming quarters.

Superior network speed and repeated 5G recognition can reinforce customer acquisition, retention, and premium-plan adoption. This infrastructure advantage is strategically durable because it supports wireless, broadband, enterprise, and emerging connected-device opportunities across multiple revenue streams.

Raised service revenue, EBITDA, and free cash flow targets show that customer growth and monetization are translating into expanding financial capacity. The outlook is supported by postpaid accounts, ARPA, 5G broadband, fiber, and premium-plan adoption, broadening the company’s recurring growth base.

bear.b: The large debt burden and declining equity base reduce balance-sheet flexibility even as profitability improves. Leverage can constrain capital allocation, increase sensitivity to refinancing and interest costs, and limit the company’s ability to absorb operating setbacks while funding network and spectrum needs.

Declining wholesale revenue and weakening prepaid trends create persistent pressure on service growth and customer mix. These areas can dilute momentum from postpaid expansion, require additional retention or acquisition investment, and make future revenue growth more dependent on premium customers and newer broadband offerings.

bear.t: Higher structural churn in broadband mix
bear.b: A growing mix of broadband-only and fiber-only accounts may raise overall account churn because these customers leave at higher rates than postpaid phone users. Higher churn can increase acquisition and retention costs, weaken customer lifetime value, and complicate the conversion of broadband growth into durable profitability.
